extracted.intended_audience: general readers and aspiring horror writers interested in Stephen King and the craft of writing
extracted.subtask_description: An author-interview style discussion about Stephen King's views on writing (especially horror), how life experiences feed fiction, and references to his craft-focused memoir 'On Writing.' Useful background for aspiring horror writers or readers studying King's approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use life experiences as material
rubrics_metrics.description: "It has given me some new things to write about and some new experiences to put in stories,"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: King states that real-life events (even traumatic ones) provide new material and experiences to incorporate into fiction. Example: his near-fatal accident supplied fresh experiences he expected to use in future stories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain your established approach to writing despite life events
rubrics_metrics.description: "he said it didn't change the way he approached his writing."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even after major personal upheaval, King's fundamental writing method and approach remained consistent; the advice implies steadiness of practice and process rather than letting circumstance radically alter craft routines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing can aid recovery and processing of trauma
rubrics_metrics.description: The piece notes that "writing helped his recovery process."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond producing stories, King frames writing as a therapeutic or rehabilitative activity — using creative work to process emotions and events. This suggests valuing writing's personal/psychological functions, not just commercial or aesthetic outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study craft-focused memoirs and resources (read 'On Writing')
rubrics_metrics.description: The article promotes King's book On Writing: A Memoir of the Craft as both a reflection on his craft and his accident.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: King's memoir is presented as a direct source of practical advice on writing. The page highlights the book (10th-anniversary edition) as a recommended resource for writers wanting concrete guidance from an experienced practitioner.
